GRADE 8 MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Time: 64 minutes

INSTRUCTIONS
1. Answer all questions.
2. Use neat handwriting.
2. For multiple choice, write the correct letter only.
3. For short answers, write clearly in the spaces provided.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A: Multiple Choice

1. About Integers at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. identify integers in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Integers completely.
   C. Integers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Integers.

2. About Integers using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. represent integers on a number line in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Integers completely.
   C. Integers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Integers.

3. About Integers when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. carry out operations of addition and subtraction integers on the number line in real life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Integers completely.
   C. Integers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Integers.

5. About Fractions at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. work out reciprocal of fractions in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

6. About Fractions using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. carry out combined operations on fractions in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

7. About Fractions when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. work out reciprocal of fractions in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

9. About Decimals at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. convert fractions to decimals in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

10. About Decimals using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. identify recurring decimals in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

11. About Decimals when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. convert recurring decimals into fractions in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

13. About Squares and Square roots at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the squares of numbers from tables in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Squares and Square roots completely.
   C. Squares and Square roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Squares and Square roots.

14. About Squares and Square roots using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the square roots of numbers from tables in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Squares and Square roots completely.
   C. Squares and Square roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Squares and Square roots.

15. About Squares and Square roots when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. work out squares and square roots of numbers using a calculator in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Squares and Square roots completely.
   C. Squares and Square roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Squares and Square roots.

17. About Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. identify rates in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages completely.
   C. Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages.

18. About Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. work out rates in real-life situations.
   B. Learners should ignore Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages completely.
   C. Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages.

19. About Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. express fractions as ratios in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages completely.
   C. Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages.

21. About Algebraic Expressions at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. factorise algebraic expressions in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Algebraic Expressions completely.
   C. Algebraic Expressions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Algebraic Expressions.

22. About Algebraic Expressions using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. simplify algebraic fractions in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Algebraic Expressions completely.
   C. Algebraic Expressions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Algebraic Expressions.

23. About Algebraic Expressions when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. evaluate algebraic expressions by substituting numerical values in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Algebraic Expressions completely.
   C. Algebraic Expressions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Algebraic Expressions.

25. About Linear Equations at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. form linear equations in two unknowns in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Equations completely.
   C. Linear Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Equations.

26. About Linear Equations using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. solve linear equations in two unknowns by substitution method in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Equations completely.
   C. Linear Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Equations.

27. About Linear Equations when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. solve linear equations in two unknowns by elimination method in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Equations completely.
   C. Linear Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Equations.

29. About Circles at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the circumference of a circle in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Circles completely.
   C. Circles is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Circles.

30. About Circles using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the length of an Arc of a circle in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Circles completely.
   C. Circles is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Circles.

31. About Circles when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. calculate the perimeter of a sector of a circle in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Circles completely.
   C. Circles is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Circles.

SECTION B: Short Answers

4. Give two examples of how you can use Integers at the market in your county.

8. Give two examples of how you can use Fractions at the market in your county.

12. Give two examples of how you can use Decimals at the market in your county.

16. Give two examples of how you can use Squares and Square roots at the market in your county.

20. Give two examples of how you can use Rates, Ratio, Proportions and Percentages at the market in your county.

24. Give two examples of how you can use Algebraic Expressions at the market in your county.

28. Give two examples of how you can use Linear Equations at the market in your county.

32. Give two examples of how you can use Circles at the market in your county.
